[tool: bash]
I wrote `/tmp/obench-cell-f7lpjlhg/bench_opencode_polyglot-rust-c_3e2mpv7q/polyglot/main.rs`. It compiles and runs under both `rustc` and `g++ -x c++`. I tested both with N = 0, 1, 2, 10 and 100, and the outputs matched. For example, f(10) is 89 and f(100) is 573147844013817084101.

It works by using a `//\` line, which the two compilers read differently. In C++ the trailing backslash continues the comment onto the next line, so that line is hidden. In Rust the next line is ordinary code. The C++ `main` sits inside a Rust block comment (`/*` … `*/`) that C++ also treats as a comment. The Rust `main` is on a single line right after a `//\`.

Both versions use 128-bit integers, so the results are correct up to about f(185). Past that the Rust version panics on overflow in a debug build, and the C++ version wraps around.
